subtitle: Lesson 4 · Q# Language Fundamentals

steps.label: use allocates a qubit
steps.sub: Every qubit starts in |0> — a guarantee of the language

steps.label: H puts it into superposition
steps.sub: In exact amplitude terms, not an approximation

steps.label: M collapses it to a Result
steps.sub: Either Zero or One — measurement is irreversible

steps.label: One shot tells you nothing
steps.sub: Only many shots reveal the real distribution

caption: Squaring each amplitude gives exactly 0.5 and 0.5 — genuinely equally likely, not approximately.

eyebrow: The whole operation, start to finish
caption: use allocates q in |0>, H superposes it, M collapses and returns the Result, Reset leaves q in a known state.

code:
import qsharp
qsharp.eval(open("MeasureSuperposition.qs").read())
results = qsharp.run("FirstOperation.MeasureSuperposition()", shots=1000)
# results is a list of 1000 Result values; roughly half Zero, half One
caption: The VS Code Run lens executes one shot by default — shots=1000 from Python is what actually shows the 50/50 split.
